approved_text: For ε > 0, let N(ε) be the fewest rotations about the origin of {(x, y) ∈ R^2 : dist(x, Z) ≤ ε} covering R^2. Find an explicit B(ε) such that, for some C > 0 and all small enough ε > 0, N(ε) ≤ B(ε) < exp(exp(exp(ε^(-C)))).
draft: For ε > 0, let N(ε) be the minimum number of copies of the set {(x, y) ∈ R^2 : dist(x, Z) ≤ ε}, rotated about the origin, needed to cover R^2. Find an explicit bound B(ε) with N(ε) ≤ B(ε) such that, for some C > 0 and all sufficiently small ε, B(ε) < exp(exp(exp(ε^(-C)))).
source_docstrings:
How many rotated (about the origin) copies of the 'pyjama set'
$\\{(x, y) \in \mathbb{R}^2 : \text{dist}(x, \mathbb{Z}) \leq \varepsilon\\}$ are needed to cover
$\mathbb{R}^2$?

In particular, can one find a better bound than the best-known bound from [KrLe25]?
source_lean:
theorem green_41 :
    ∃ C : ℝ, C > 0 ∧ ∃ ε₀ > 0, ∀ ε ∈ Ioc 0 ε₀,
      let ans := (answer(sorry) : ℝ)
      (minCopies ε : ℝ) ≤ ans ∧ ans < Real.exp (Real.exp (Real.exp (ε ^ (-C))))
